properties.doc: Returns the position on the clicked feature, that is close to the click position. For points it will always be the center position, for lines it will be the closest point on the line, for billboards it will be the anchor point and for polygons it's equal to getClickPos().

properties.name: featureId
properties.doc: Returns the id of the clicked feature.

properties.name: featureLayerName
properties.doc: Returns the name of the layer of the clicked feature. Note that this is the layer name in the tile, not the name of style layer.

properties.name: featurePos
properties.doc: Returns the position of the clicked feature. For a MultiPoint this is the point that was clicked, not the centre of the whole set - which getFeatureClickPos deliberately does not cover, and which a caller otherwise has to reconstruct from getFeaturePosIndex plus a downcast.

properties.name: featurePosIndex
properties.doc: In case of MultiPoint PointGeometry this will return the index of the clicked position

properties.name: layer
properties.doc: Returns the layer of the vector tile.

properties.name: mapTile
properties.doc: Returns the tile id of the clicked feature.

properties.name: id
properties.doc: Returns the id of the feature.

properties.name: layerName
properties.doc: Returns the layer name of the feature.

properties.name: mapTile
properties.doc: Returns the map tile of the feature.

properties.name: id
properties.doc: Returns the id of the builder.

properties.name: layerName
properties.doc: Returns the layer name of the builder.

properties.name: mapTile
properties.doc: Returns the map tile of the builder.

properties.name: buildingRenderOrder
properties.doc: Returns the current display order of the buildings.

properties.name: clickHandlerLayerFilter
properties.doc: Returns the click handler layer filter. The filter is given as ECMA regular expression that is applied to qualified layer names.

properties.name: clickRadius
properties.doc: Returns the click radius of vector tile features. Units are screen density independent pixels (DP or DIP).

properties.name: labelBlendingSpeed
properties.doc: Returns the current relative label blending speed.

properties.name: labelRenderOrder
properties.doc: Returns the current display order of the labels.

properties.name: layerBlendingSpeed
properties.doc: Returns the current relative layer blending speed.

properties.name: rendererLayerFilter
properties.doc: Returns the renderer layer filter. The filter is given as ECMA regular expression that is applied to qualified layer names.

properties.name: tileCacheCapacity
properties.doc: Returns the tile cache capacity.

properties.name: tileDecoder
properties.doc: Returns the tile decoder assigned to this layer.

properties.name: vectorTileEventListener
properties.doc: Returns the vector tile event listener.

properties.name: dataSource
properties.doc: Returns the tile data source of the search service.

properties.name: layers
properties.doc: Returns the layers to filter while decoding tiles.

properties.name: maxResults
properties.doc: Returns the maximum number of results the search service returns.

properties.name: maxZoom
properties.doc: Returns the maximum zoom level of vector tiles used. By default the maximum zoom level is specified by data source.

properties.name: minZoom
properties.doc: Returns the minimum zoom level of vector tiles used. By default the minimum zoom level is specified by data source and is usually 0.

properties.name: preventDuplicates
properties.doc: Returns wether to prevent duplicate elements

properties.name: projection
properties.doc: Returns the projection the results are expressed in, which is the data source's.

properties.name: sortByDistance
properties.doc: Returns wether result features are sorted by distance

properties.name: tileDecoder
properties.doc: Returns the tile decoder used by the search service.

properties.name: DPI
properties.doc: Returns the dots per inch parameter of the screen.

properties.name: DPToPX
properties.doc: Returns a value that is used for converting display independent pixels (dp) to pixels (px). This values depends on the screen density.

properties.name: FOVY
properties.doc: Returns the vertical field of view angle.

properties.name: aspectRatio
properties.doc: Returns the aspect ratio of the map screen. Equal to width / height.

properties.name: cameraChanged
properties.doc: Returns the state of the camera changed flag.

properties.name: far
properties.doc: Returns the far plane distance.

properties.name: height
properties.doc: Returns the height of the map screen.

properties.name: near
properties.doc: Returns the near plane distance.

properties.name: rotation
properties.doc: Returns the camera rotation angle.

properties.name: screenHeight
properties.doc: Returns the screen height.

properties.name: screenWidth
properties.doc: Returns the screen width.

properties.name: tilt
properties.doc: Returns the camera tilt angle. A NEGATIVE tilt means the view looks above the horizon.

properties.name: unitToDPCoef
properties.doc: Returns the conversion ratio between internal map units and screen density independent pixels (DP or DIP). This parameter is dependent on the zoom level, DPI and other screen parameters.

properties.name: unitToPXCoef
properties.doc: Returns the conversion ratio between internal map units and screen pixels. This parameter is dependent on the zoom level and other screen parameters.

properties.name: width
properties.doc: Returns the width of the map screen.

properties.name: zoom
properties.doc: Returns the camera zoom level.

properties.name: zoom0Distance
properties.doc: Returns the distance between the focus and the camera position, when the zoom level is set to 0. This parameter depends on the screen size, DPI, tile draw size and field of view settings.

properties.name: bigEndian
properties.doc: Returns the endianness of output format.

properties.name: z
properties.doc: Returns the state of Z coordinate serialization.

properties.name: z
properties.doc: Returns the state of Z coordinate serialization.

massif::AnimationType::AnimationType.name: ANIMATION_TYPE_STEP
massif::AnimationType::AnimationType.doc: Step transition is applied at the middle of the animation.

massif::AnimationType::AnimationType.name: ANIMATION_TYPE_LINEAR
massif::AnimationType::AnimationType.doc: Linear transition is used for animation.

massif::AnimationType::AnimationType.name: ANIMATION_TYPE_SMOOTHSTEP
massif::AnimationType::AnimationType.doc: Smooth transition with 2nd order continuity is used for animation.

massif::AnimationType::AnimationType.name: ANIMATION_TYPE_SPRING
massif::AnimationType::AnimationType.doc: Spring-like transition is used for animation.

massif::BillboardOrientation::BillboardO.name: BILLBOARD_ORIENTATION_FACE_CAMERA
massif::BillboardOrientation::BillboardO.doc: Billboard always faces the camera plane, regardless of rotation.

massif::BillboardOrientation::BillboardO.name: BILLBOARD_ORIENTATION_FACE_CAMERA_GROUND
massif::BillboardOrientation::BillboardO.doc: Billboard lies parallel to the ground and rotates around it's anchor point to face the camera. SetRotation can be used to offset the final angle of the billboard.

massif::BillboardOrientation::BillboardO.name: BILLBOARD_ORIENTATION_GROUND
massif::BillboardOrientation::BillboardO.doc: Billboard lies on the ground, orientation does not depend on the camera position.

massif::BillboardScaling::BillboardScali.name: BILLBOARD_SCALING_WORLD_SIZE
massif::BillboardScaling::BillboardScali.doc: Billboard has a constant world space size. Zooming causes the billboard to get smaller or bigger on the screen.

massif::BillboardScaling::BillboardScali.name: BILLBOARD_SCALING_SCREEN_SIZE
massif::BillboardScaling::BillboardScali.doc: Billboard's size on screen is unaffected by zooming, but billboards that are further away from the camera get smaller when the tilt angle is < 90.

massif::BillboardScaling::BillboardScali.name: BILLBOARD_SCALING_CONST_SCREEN_SIZE
massif::BillboardScaling::BillboardScali.doc: Billboard's screen size is always the same, regardless of the zoom level, tilt angle or billboard's position.

massif::ClickType::ClickType.name: CLICK_TYPE_SINGLE
massif::ClickType::ClickType.doc: A click caused by pressing down and then releasing the screen.

massif::ClickType::ClickType.name: CLICK_TYPE_LONG
massif::ClickType::ClickType.doc: A click caused by pressing down but not releasing the screen.

massif::ClickType::ClickType.name: CLICK_TYPE_DOUBLE
massif::ClickType::ClickType.doc: A click caused by two fast consecutive taps on the screen.

massif::ClickType::ClickType.name: CLICK_TYPE_DUAL
massif::ClickType::ClickType.doc: A click caused by two simultaneous taps on the screen.

massif::ClusterBuilderMode::ClusterBuild.name: CLUSTER_BUILDER_MODE_ELEMENTS
massif::ClusterBuilderMode::ClusterBuild.doc: Cluster builder receives full list of elements in the cluster. This mode is more expensive compared to the light mode.

massif::ClusterBuilderMode::ClusterBuild.name: CLUSTER_BUILDER_MODE_ELEMENT_COUNT
massif::ClusterBuilderMode::ClusterBuild.doc: Cluster builder receives element count in the cluster. This mode is less expensive compared to the full mode.

massif::ColorFormat::ColorFormat.name: COLOR_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED
massif::ColorFormat::ColorFormat.doc: Options for identifiny unsupported image formats.

massif::ColorFormat::ColorFormat.name: COLOR_FORMAT_BGRA
massif::ColorFormat::ColorFormat.doc: An image format that describes images with four channels, one for each color: blue, green and red and one for alpha. This color format will be converted to RGBA.

massif::ColorFormat::ColorFormat.name: COLOR_FORMAT_RGBA_4444
massif::ColorFormat::ColorFormat.doc: An image format that describes images with four channels, one for each color: red, green, and blue and one for alpha. Each color is only four bits. This color format will be converted to RGBA.

massif::ColorFormat::ColorFormat.name: COLOR_FORMAT_RGB_565
massif::ColorFormat::ColorFormat.doc: An image format that describes images with three channels, one for each color: red, green, and blue. Red and blue colors are each packed into 5 bits, green into 6 bits. This color format will be converted to RGB.

massif::CompositeSourceType::CompositeSo.name: COMPOSITE_SOURCE_TYPE_RASTER
massif::CompositeSourceType::CompositeSo.doc: A raster tile source, drawn as a RasterTileLayer at its style slot.

massif::CompositeSourceType::CompositeSo.name: COMPOSITE_SOURCE_TYPE_HILLSHADE
massif::CompositeSourceType::CompositeSo.doc: An RGB-encoded elevation source, drawn as a HillshadeRasterTileLayer at its style slot.

massif::CompositeSourceType::CompositeSo.name: COMPOSITE_SOURCE_TYPE_VECTOR
massif::CompositeSourceType::CompositeSo.doc: Another MBVT/protobuf source (including ContourTileDataSource), drawn at its style slot as its own child VectorTileLayer using the master decoder, filtered to its own layer name. Kept separate (not merged) so it overzooms independently via its own MaxOverzoomLevel and does not need the DEM at the target zoom.

massif::FreeRoamMode::FreeRoamMode.name: FREE_ROAM_MODE_OFF
massif::FreeRoamMode::FreeRoamMode.doc: Off: the standard map gestures. A one-finger drag pans the map.

massif::FreeRoamMode::FreeRoamMode.name: FREE_ROAM_MODE_LOOK
massif::FreeRoamMode::FreeRoamMode.doc: Look: a one-finger drag looks around instead of panning - sideways turns the heading about the camera, up and down tilts the map the way the two-finger tilt does, so the camera still orbits its focus point. Panning moves to a two-finger drag; pinch and two-finger rotation are unchanged.

massif::FreeRoamMode::FreeRoamMode.name: FREE_ROAM_MODE_FIRST_PERSON
massif::FreeRoamMode::FreeRoamMode.doc: First person: the camera stops orbiting anything. A one-finger drag turns the view about the CAMERA on both axes, like a mouse in a first person game - the position never changes - and a two-finger drag moves, forward/back and strafing, the way the keys would. Pinch and two-finger rotation are off, since neither belongs to that control scheme. The camera model applies to every source, not just to touch: setTilt and setMapRotation turn the view in place too, so a camera driven by the device's orientation behaves exactly like the drag.

massif::GeometryType::GeometryType.name: GEOMETRY_TYPE_POLYGON
massif::GeometryType::GeometryType.doc: An outer ring and any number of holes.

massif::HillshadeMethod::HillshadeMethod.name: COMBINED
massif::HillshadeMethod::HillshadeMethod.doc: Combined hillshade algorithm based on GDAL.

massif::HillshadeMethod::HillshadeMethod.name: IGOR
massif::HillshadeMethod::HillshadeMethod.doc: Igor hillshade algorithm based on GDAL.

massif::HillshadeMethod::HillshadeMethod.name: MULTIDIRECTIONAL
massif::HillshadeMethod::HillshadeMethod.doc: Multi-directional hillshade based on GDAL: four light sources at 225, 270, 315 and 360 degrees weighted by the aspect. Ignores the illumination azimuth, uses only its altitude.

massif::HillshadeMethod::HillshadeMethod.name: BASIC
massif::HillshadeMethod::HillshadeMethod.doc: Basic hillshade algorithm based on GDAL.

massif::LineEndType::LineEndType.name: LINE_END_TYPE_NONE
massif::LineEndType::LineEndType.doc: No line end points are drawn.

massif::LineEndType::LineEndType.name: LINE_END_TYPE_SQUARE
massif::LineEndType::LineEndType.doc: Line end points are drawn as squares.

massif::LineEndType::LineEndType.name: LINE_END_TYPE_ROUND
massif::LineEndType::LineEndType.doc: Line end points are drawn as half circles.

massif::LineJoinType::LineJoinType.name: LINE_JOIN_TYPE_NONE
massif::LineJoinType::LineJoinType.doc: Line segments are not connected with each other. The fastest and ugliest.

massif::LineJoinType::LineJoinType.name: LINE_JOIN_TYPE_MITER
massif::LineJoinType::LineJoinType.doc: Line segments are connected with each other using miter connections. This is the preferred mode (fast and good looking generally).

massif::LineJoinType::LineJoinType.name: LINE_JOIN_TYPE_BEVEL
massif::LineJoinType::LineJoinType.doc: Line segments are connected with each other using bevel (straight line) connectors. Fast but results in an unnatural line.

massif::LineJoinType::LineJoinType.name: LINE_JOIN_TYPE_ROUND
massif::LineJoinType::LineJoinType.doc: Line segments are connected with each other using circle sectors resulting in round corners. Slowest and prettiest.

massif::LocalSpatialIndexType::LocalSpat.name: LOCAL_SPATIAL_INDEX_TYPE_NULL
massif::LocalSpatialIndexType::LocalSpat.doc: Null index, fastest if few elements are used. No element culling is performed.

massif::LocalSpatialIndexType::LocalSpat.name: LOCAL_SPATIAL_INDEX_TYPE_KDTREE
massif::LocalSpatialIndexType::LocalSpat.doc: K-d tree index, element culling is exact and fast.

massif::MBTilesScheme::MBTilesScheme.name: MBTILES_SCHEME_TMS
massif::MBTilesScheme::MBTilesScheme.doc: The default scheme. Vertical coordinate is not flipped.

massif::MBTilesScheme::MBTilesScheme.name: MBTILES_SCHEME_XYZ
massif::MBTilesScheme::MBTilesScheme.doc: Alternative to TMS scheme. Vertical coordinate is flipped.

massif::PackageAction::PackageAction.name: PACKAGE_ACTION_WAITING
massif::PackageAction::PackageAction.doc: Package is waiting in the task queue.

massif::PackageErrorType::PackageErrorTy.name: PACKAGE_ERROR_TYPE_DOWNLOAD_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
massif::PackageErrorType::PackageErrorTy.doc: The number of downloaded packages exceeded subscription limit.

massif::PackageErrorType::PackageErrorTy.name: PACKAGE_ERROR_TYPE_PACKAGE_TOO_BIG
massif::PackageErrorType::PackageErrorTy.doc: The bounding box of the package contains too many tiles. This error is only returned for custom bounding box packages.

massif::PackageErrorType::PackageErrorTy.name: PACKAGE_ERROR_TYPE_NO_OFFLINE_PLAN
massif::PackageErrorType::PackageErrorTy.doc: The license does not allow downloading offline packages.

massif::PackageTileStatus::PackageTileSt.name: PACKAGE_TILE_STATUS_MISSING
massif::PackageTileStatus::PackageTileSt.doc: Tile is not part of the package.

massif::PackageTileStatus::PackageTileSt.name: PACKAGE_TILE_STATUS_PARTIAL
massif::PackageTileStatus::PackageTileSt.doc: Tile is part of the package, but package does not fully cover it. This value is no longer used, thus this is deprecated.

massif::PackageTileStatus::PackageTileSt.name: PACKAGE_TILE_STATUS_FULL
massif::PackageTileStatus::PackageTileSt.doc: Tile if part of the package and package fully covers it.

massif::PanningMode::PanningMode.name: PANNING_MODE_FREE
massif::PanningMode::PanningMode.doc: Free panning means that the map panning is unrestricted, user is able to zoom, rotate and pan the map at the same time without any artificial limits.

massif::PanningMode::PanningMode.name: PANNING_MODE_STICKY
massif::PanningMode::PanningMode.doc: Sticky panning means that the map panning is restricted, user is able to freely pan the map, but zooming and rotating gestures can't be performed at the same time. User is still able to switch between zooming and rotating the map but it takes a bit more effort compared to FREE panning. gesture is performed and

massif::PanningMode::PanningMode.name: PANNING_MODE_STICKY_FINAL
massif::PanningMode::PanningMode.doc: Final sticky panning means that the map panning is restricted, user is able to freely pan the map, but zooming and rotating gestures can't be performed at the same time. Once the gesture type is determined the user is stuck with either zooming or rotating. To switch the gesture the user has to lift at least one the two fingers off the screen.

massif::PanningSpeedMode::PanningSpeedMo.name: PANNING_SPEED_MODE_MAP
massif::PanningSpeedMode::PanningSpeedMo.doc: The map point under the finger follows it exactly, which is what a flat map does. On a tilted view the speed then changes DURING the gesture: a drag that starts near the camera and travels up the screen accelerates as the finger reaches parts of the screen that are further away.

massif::PanningSpeedMode::PanningSpeedMo.name: PANNING_SPEED_MODE_ANCHORED
massif::PanningSpeedMode::PanningSpeedMo.doc: The scale is measured where the pan STARTS and stays fixed for the whole gesture: starting far away still pans fast and starting close still pans slowly, but the speed never changes while the finger is down. The default.

massif::PanningSpeedMode::PanningSpeedMo.name: PANNING_SPEED_MODE_CONSTANT
massif::PanningSpeedMode::PanningSpeedMo.doc: The scale is measured at the centre of the screen, so it depends neither on where the finger started nor on where it goes - every pan moves the map at the same rate.

massif::PivotMode::PivotMode.name: PIVOT_MODE_TOUCHPOINT
massif::PivotMode::PivotMode.doc: The touch point (or middle point between 2 finger touches) is used as the pivot point.

massif::PivotMode::PivotMode.name: PIVOT_MODE_CENTERPOINT
massif::PivotMode::PivotMode.doc: Screen center is always used for pivot point.

massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.name: ROUTING_ACTION_NO_TURN
massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.doc: Continue along the given street, do not turn.

massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.name: ROUTING_ACTION_REACH_VIA_LOCATION
massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.doc: Reached given via point. If this is the final point, FINISH action is used instead.

massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.name: ROUTING_ACTION_ENTER_ROUNDABOUT
massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.doc: Enter roundabout. Used by Valhalla and OSRM.

massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.name: ROUTING_ACTION_LEAVE_ROUNDABOUT
massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.doc: Leave roundabout. Used by Valhalla and OSRM.

massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.name: ROUTING_ACTION_STAY_ON_ROUNDABOUT
massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.doc: Continue along the roundabout. Only used by OSRM.

massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.name: ROUTING_ACTION_START_AT_END_OF_STREET
massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.doc: Start at the end of the street. Currently used only by OSRM.

massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.name: ROUTING_ACTION_ENTER_AGAINST_ALLOWED_DIRECTION
massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.doc: Enter street while moving against the allowed direction. Only used by OSRM.

massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.name: ROUTING_ACTION_LEAVE_AGAINST_ALLOWED_DIRECTION
massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.doc: Leave the street while moving aginst the allowed direction. Only used by OSRM.

massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.name: ROUTING_ACTION_GO_UP
massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.doc: Go up. Only used by the SGRE.

massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.name: ROUTING_ACTION_GO_DOWN
massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.doc: Go down. Only used by SGRE.

massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.name: ROUTING_ACTION_ENTER_FERRY
massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.doc: Enter ferry. Only used by Valhalla.

massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.name: ROUTING_ACTION_LEAVE_FERRY
massif::RoutingAction::RoutingAction.doc: Leave ferry. Only used by Valhalla.

massif::TileFormat::TileFormat.name: TILE_FORMAT_AUTO
massif::TileFormat::TileFormat.doc: Detect the format from the tile data. The two are unambiguous in practice, but set the format explicitly when the source is known - it skips the check and cannot be fooled.

massif::TileFormat::TileFormat.name: TILE_FORMAT_MVT
massif::TileFormat::TileFormat.doc: MapBox Vector Tile, the protobuf format.

massif::TileFormat::TileFormat.name: TILE_FORMAT_MLT
massif::TileFormat::TileFormat.doc: MapLibre Tile, the columnar format. Smaller tiles and faster decoding, but the whole tile is decoded at once - MVT decodes only the layers and attributes the style asks for.

massif::TileSubstitutionPolicy::TileSubs.name: TILE_SUBSTITUTION_POLICY_VISIBLE
massif::TileSubstitutionPolicy::TileSubs.doc: Consider only tiles that are currently visible. This is recommended for low-latency data sources, like offline sources.

massif::VectorElementDragMode::VectorEle.name: VECTOR_ELEMENT_DRAG_MODE_VERTEX
massif::VectorElementDragMode::VectorEle.doc: A single vertex is being moved.

massif::VectorElementDragMode::VectorEle.name: VECTOR_ELEMENT_DRAG_MODE_ELEMENT
massif::VectorElementDragMode::VectorEle.doc: The whole vector element is being moved.

massif::VectorElementDragPointStyle::Vec.name: VECTOR_ELEMENT_DRAG_POINT_STYLE_NORMAL
massif::VectorElementDragPointStyle::Vec.doc: Normal control point. Corresponds to vertex.

massif::VectorElementDragPointStyle::Vec.name: VECTOR_ELEMENT_DRAG_POINT_STYLE_VIRTUAL
massif::VectorElementDragPointStyle::Vec.doc: Virtual control point (midpoint between actual vertices). Used for lines and polygons.

massif::VectorElementDragResult::VectorE.name: VECTOR_ELEMENT_DRAG_RESULT_IGNORE
massif::VectorElementDragResult::VectorE.doc: Dragging should be ignored. The input event will be passed on to other handlers.

massif::VectorElementDragResult::VectorE.name: VECTOR_ELEMENT_DRAG_RESULT_STOP
massif::VectorElementDragResult::VectorE.doc: Dragging should be ignored. The input event is not passed on to other handlers.

massif::VectorElementDragResult::VectorE.name: VECTOR_ELEMENT_DRAG_RESULT_MODIFY
massif::VectorElementDragResult::VectorE.doc: The underlying vector element (or vertex) should be modified.

massif::VectorElementDragResult::VectorE.name: VECTOR_ELEMENT_DRAG_RESULT_DELETE
massif::VectorElementDragResult::VectorE.doc: The underlying vector element or vertex should be deleted.

massif::VectorTileRenderOrder::VectorTil.name: VECTOR_TILE_RENDER_ORDER_LAYER
massif::VectorTileRenderOrder::VectorTil.doc: Elements are rendered together with the same layer elements. Layers that are on top of the layers are rendered on top this layer.

massif::VectorTileRenderOrder::VectorTil.name: VECTOR_TILE_RENDER_ORDER_LAST
massif::VectorTileRenderOrder::VectorTil.doc: Elements are rendered on top of all normal layers.
